newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso strengthens on dollar inflow.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso strengthens on dollar inflow.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended firmer at 26.287 to the dollar from Friday's close of 26.290 on larger dollar inflows, traders said.
"There was an influx of dollars from offshore funds. They want to lock in local Treasury bills and bonds before rates go down further," one trader said.
Banks sold their dollars to participate in the T-bills auction as well as buy debt papers in the secondary market, he said.

Money swamped the primary auction which pulled down the average interest rates across all maturities. Bankers expected the rates to slip further after the Central Bank cut its reserve requirements on banks' deposits.
A total of 38.37 billion pesos worth of bids was received by the auction committee, but it only awarded 4.5 billion pesos worth of bills.
The Central Bank intervened by buying dollars at 26.285 to 26.288. Traders estimated the Central Bank's purchases at around $50 million.
Turnover in the market reached $178 million, lower than Friday's $246.20 million.
Done rates ranged from 26.285 to 26.289. Oil companies bought $10 million at 26.287.
Traders expected the peso to remain steady at the current levels due to the Central Bank's intervention.
